oracle_provenance: Standard textbook GD&T tolerance-analysis identities (worst-case sum, RSS root-sum-square); RSS formula sanity-checked independently against the classic 3-4-5 right-triangle identity (sqrt(3^2+4^2)=5) before implementation; not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded worst-case and RSS dimensional tolerance stack-up from declared contributor tolerances; not measured process capability (Cpk) or physical assembled-sample verification.

cases.question: When worst-case stack exceeds the limit but the RSS stack does not, is that reported as a distinct, defensible middle-ground disposition rather than a simple pass/fail?
Just above the exact RSS value for a tighter three-contributor stack, does the RSS check still pass while worst-case fails?
When contributor tolerances are so large that even the RSS stack exceeds the limit, is that flagged as failing statistically, not just at worst-case?
Must a stack-up with fewer than the minimum two independent contributors be rejected rather than silently computed?

For comfortably small contributors well inside spec, does RSS still strictly discriminate below worst-case (as the model's own math guarantees for more than one nonzero contributor), rather than the two collapsing to the same value?
